topic: Figarland Garling orchestrated and profited from the God Valley Incident, and the World Government rewarded him with decades of promotions instead of punishment
title: Garling Led God Valley, Then Got Promoted For It
description:
Figarland Garling found the Davy Family, picked God Valley as the site of a World Noble hunting competition, and abandoned the mother of his own sons to fall. Thirty-eight years later, he's one of the Five Elders. Here's the chapter-by-chapter record of a man who was never punished for any of it, only promoted.

From the Native Hunting Competition to the fight he arrived late to finish, this traces every step of Garling's rise, and what it cost the son he left behind in a treasure chest.
comment: Was Garling ever actually the hero of God Valley, or just the last man standing when the credit got handed out?

lines.text: Figarland Garling led the hunt at God Valley, and the World Government's reward was a promotion, not a punishment.

shot.fallback: golden armored noble standing over a ruined island

lines.text: Thirty-eight years later, that same man sits as one of the Five Elders, the second-highest authority on the planet.

shot.fallback: elder noble seated in a chamber of power

lines.text: So how does the man who designed that entire nightmare end up climbing instead of falling?

shot.fallback: ambitious figure rising instead of falling

lines.text: Every single step of that long climb is on record, chapter by chapter, for anyone willing to actually look...

shot.fallback: documented history laid out clearly

lines.text: And it all starts with Garling finding something he was never actually supposed to find at all...

shot.fallback: noble uncovering a hidden secret

lines.text: Forty years ago, Garling and his fellow Knights of God stopped at an island called God Valley on routine assignment.

shot.search: Garling Knights of God God Valley arrival
shot.fallback: armored knights arriving at a lush island

lines.text: He found vast natural resources there, and something far more valuable to the World Government: the hidden Davy Family.

shot.fallback: noble uncovering a hidden family

lines.text: Chapter 1158 says the island refused to join the World Government when Garling offered them membership.

shot.search: God Valley refuses World Government offer
shot.fallback: island leaders rejecting a government offer

lines.text: That refusal, plus the Davy Family, plus a name the Celestial Dragons considered blasphemous, became Garling's pretext.

shot.fallback: noble building a convenient justification

lines.text: None of that was really about blasphemy at all. It was about an excuse convenient enough that nobody above him would ask questions.

shot.fallback: noble crafting a convenient cover story

lines.text: He proposed hosting the World Nobles' next Native Hunting Competition right there, on God Valley itself.

shot.fallback: noble proposing a cruel competition

lines.text: A hundred thousand civilians would be marked as targets. Garling is the one who picked the venue.

shot.search: Civilians marked targets Garling picks venue
shot.fallback: vast crowd marked as unwilling targets

lines.text: He didn't just discover the Davy Family. He turned that discovery into the single biggest opportunity of his entire career.

shot.fallback: ambitious noble seizing a rare opportunity

lines.text: To prepare, Garling orders Marines under his command to round up the local population using tranquilizer rounds, disguised as a training exercise.

shot.fallback: soldiers quietly rounding up a population

lines.text: A young cadet named Monkey D. Dragon is one of the soldiers carrying out that very order, long before he ever becomes a revolutionary.

shot.search: Dragon young cadet carries out order
shot.fallback: unaware young soldier following dark orders

lines.text: The giant King Harald, who befriends Rocks around this same time, has no idea Garling's whole plan is already in motion...

shot.fallback: giant king unknowingly near a hidden plot

lines.text: Before any of that, Garling met a local woman named Magnolia, and she had no idea who he really was.

shot.fallback: noble meeting an unsuspecting local woman

lines.text: She fell for him anyway, and a year later she gave birth to his twin sons: Shamrock and Shanks.

shot.fallback: mother holding newborn twin sons

lines.text: Magnolia believed Garling would come back for good, that they'd live together on the island as a real family.

shot.fallback: hopeful mother waiting for a promise

lines.text: Garling never told her he was a World Noble at all. He let her build an entire future on a lie she never knew she was living.

shot.fallback: noble concealing his true identity

lines.text: For a year, she raised two sons alone, believing their father was simply away, not that he ruled over her entire world.

shot.fallback: devoted mother raising children alone

lines.text: Chapter 1160 shows exactly how little that promise meant to him when he finally did return.

shot.fallback: noble returning without any warmth

lines.text: Garling tells her, with no hesitation at all, that her home is about to be destroyed and he's marrying someone else.

shot.fallback: noble delivering devastating news coldly

lines.text: When she won't let it go, Garling strikes her down and simply walks away, leaving her for gone.

shot.fallback: noble turning away from a fallen woman

lines.text: She survives just long enough to beg a passing Marine cadet to save her sons. That cadet is Monkey D. Dragon.

shot.search: Dragon finds weakened Magnolia begs save sons
shot.fallback: young marine discovering a weakened woman

lines.text: One act of casual cruelty from Garling is the entire reason Dragon ends up holding baby Shanks at all...

shot.fallback: young marine cradling a rescued infant

lines.text: Garling doesn't even stay to confirm whether she lives or not. He simply has other, more important matters to attend to.

shot.fallback: indifferent noble walking away without looking back

lines.text: Saint Maffey is sent to track down the children afterward, treating two babies like lost property instead of family.

shot.fallback: soldier recovering children like misplaced items

lines.text: Not realizing Garling had twins, and assuming Dragon was gone too, Maffey eventually calls her mission complete anyway...

shot.fallback: agent closing a mission on false assumptions

lines.text: The competition opens with an announcement: a hundred thousand Rabbits, a hundred fifty Rare Rabbits, Shakky as the grand prize.

shot.fallback: grand announcement over a waiting crowd

lines.text: A journalist named Morgans has already leaked word of the event's prizes to half the Grand Line by this point.

shot.fallback: journalist spreading dangerous information widely

lines.text: That leak is exactly why Rocks and Roger's crews are already racing toward the island before the hunt even opens.

shot.fallback: pirate crews rushing toward an island

lines.text: Garling has no idea yet that his carefully designed game is about to collide with two of the strongest crews alive.

shot.fallback: confident noble unaware of approaching danger

lines.text: Before the timer even starts, the island's own king stands up to protest his people being used this way.

shot.fallback: brave king standing against a cruel game

lines.text: Garling strikes him down on the spot, earning a ten-thousand-point penalty for starting early.

shot.fallback: noble punishing a brave protest instantly

lines.text: He doesn't care about the penalty at all. He calls it a fair handicap to make the hunt more competitive.

shot.fallback: noble treating cruelty as sport

lines.text: Then he bickers with fellow Knight Shepherd Sommers over which of them gets to claim Shakky as a bride.

shot.fallback: two nobles arguing over a prize

lines.text: Saint Saturn himself, one of the Five Elders already, is standing right there watching the whole opening ceremony unfold.

shot.fallback: powerful elder observing the proceedings

lines.text: When the Davy Family members get paraded out as Super Rare targets, Saturn personally compliments Garling on the find.

shot.search: Saturn compliments Garling Davy Family find
shot.fallback: powerful elder praising a subordinate

lines.text: Garling brushes it off, crediting fate instead of skill, the kind of modesty that plays well in front of someone ranked above him.

shot.fallback: noble performing modesty for an elder

lines.text: Once the hunt actually starts, Garling races ahead of every other Noble, racking up a hundred thousand points almost immediately.

shot.fallback: competitive noble leading the hunt

lines.text: He targets only the highest-value people first, treating every single one of them as a number on a scoreboard.

shot.fallback: noble treating people as a scoreboard

lines.text: Among the Super Rare targets paraded out that morning are several members of the Davy Family itself, including a boy named Teach.

shot.fallback: family members paraded as valuable targets

lines.text: Teach will grow up to become Marshall D. Teach, Blackbeard, and he never forgets whose game put him on display that day.

shot.fallback: future pirate remembering a childhood humiliation

lines.text: Bartholomew Kuma is one of those high-value targets too, hunted for sport alongside everyone else on that list.

shot.fallback: young fighter marked as a prized target

lines.text: Dragon, disgusted by what he's seeing unfold, breaks his own orders to stop a Noble from finishing Kuma off.

shot.fallback: defiant soldier protecting an intended target

lines.text: That one choice from Dragon starts the chain of events that eventually builds the entire Revolutionary Army.

shot.fallback: single choice sparking a future rebellion

lines.text: Nobody watching the broadcast back in Mary Geoise doubts for a second who's about to win this entire thing.

shot.search: Mary Geoise broadcast confident Garling wins
shot.fallback: distant audience confidently watching a favorite

lines.text: He is, by every measure the World Nobles use, the clear favorite to win the entire competition...

shot.fallback: confident noble leading decisively

lines.text: Then Rocks and Roger's crews storm the island from opposite sides, and Garling's priorities reveal themselves instantly.

shot.fallback: two pirate crews invading from both sides

lines.text: He doesn't send the Marines to protect the hundred thousand civilians still trapped in that hunt.

shot.fallback: soldiers abandoning trapped civilians

lines.text: He orders them to pull back and guard the Celestial Dragons instead, leaving the Knights of God to handle the actual pirates.

shot.fallback: noble prioritizing elites over everyone else

lines.text: Chapter 1096 confirms it directly: Garling's entire chain of command exists to protect Nobles first, always.

shot.fallback: command structure protecting the powerful first

lines.text: Vice Admiral Garp arrives with reinforcements anyway, because somebody still has to actually fight for those civilians.

shot.search: Garp arrives reinforcements fights for civilians
shot.fallback: veteran marine arriving to help

lines.text: A young Marine cadet named Monkey D. Dragon is horrified by what he sees and quietly breaks from his own orders to help.

shot.search: Dragon horrified defies orders helps civilians
shot.fallback: young marine breaking ranks to help

lines.text: Garling never once breaks from his orders that day. He follows the chain of command exactly where it's always pointed: upward.

shot.fallback: noble perfectly obedient to the hierarchy

lines.text: Garling, meanwhile, goes looking for the one family he actually cares about catching: the Davy Family trying to escape.

shot.fallback: noble chasing a fleeing family

lines.text: Among the Knights sent out, Saint Maffey is tasked with one very specific job: recovering Garling's own missing sons.

shot.fallback: knight searching for missing children

lines.text: Even in the middle of a battlefield, Garling's personal interests get their own dedicated Knight of God...

shot.fallback: noble's private concerns given top priority

lines.text: Garling finally catches up to Rocks D. Xebec himself, and for a while, it looks like a real fight.

shot.fallback: noble confronting a legendary pirate

lines.text: Garling's regeneration comes from a covenant with Imu himself, letting him shrug off almost any injury like it never happened.

shot.fallback: noble's body healing from a dark covenant

lines.text: That's not strength he ever actually earned through training. That's a gift handed down by the one ruler everyone in this story is afraid of.

shot.fallback: power granted rather than earned

lines.text: Even his durability, the one thing that keeps him alive against someone like Rocks, isn't really his own either.

shot.search: Garling durability not truly his own
shot.fallback: borrowed durability keeping a noble alive

lines.text: Chapter 1162 shows Rocks' swordsmanship is powerful enough to slow down even Garling's regeneration from the Knights' power.

shot.fallback: powerful pirate overwhelming a regenerating foe

lines.text: A fellow Knight reminds Garling that taking Rocks down would please Imu greatly. Garling agrees without hesitation.

shot.fallback: noble motivated purely by pleasing a ruler

lines.text: His own overconfidence gets him and his allies badly beaten by Rocks shortly after.

shot.fallback: overconfident noble soundly defeated

lines.text: It's actually Imu who turns the tide, possessing Saturn's body and transforming Rocks into a mindless demon.

shot.fallback: shadowy ruler transforming a legendary pirate

lines.text: Before that, Rocks briefly finds his wife Eris and son Teach, trying desperately to get them off the island alive.

shot.fallback: desperate father trying to save family

lines.text: Imu, controlling his every move by then, forces Rocks to turn on the very people he was trying to save.

shot.fallback: controlled warrior turned against loved ones

lines.text: Kuma manages to pull Eris and Teach away just in time, the one mercy anybody shows that family all day.

shot.search: Kuma saves Eris Teach timely rescue
shot.fallback: hero rescuing a family at the last second

lines.text: Even then, it takes Garp and Roger together, using everything they have, to finally bring Rocks down for good.

shot.fallback: two legends combining their full strength

lines.text: By the time Rocks finally collapses, Garp and Roger are both just as exhausted, barely standing themselves.

shot.fallback: two heroes utterly spent after battle

lines.text: Garling isn't anywhere near that final struggle. He shows up only after Rocks collapses from exhaustion.

shot.fallback: noble arriving only after the real fight

lines.text: Chapter 1166 shows him approaching the downed, exhausted Rocks, flanked by two fellow Knights for safety, and finishing the job himself.

shot.fallback: noble striking a defeated, exhausted opponent

lines.text: Garp and Roger did the actual work. Garling took the one moment that mattered for the record books...

shot.search: Garp Roger real work Garling credit
shot.fallback: two heroes doing the work, one taking credit

lines.text: Here's the part that should bother you more than the fight itself: what happens right after.

shot.fallback: consequence more disturbing than the fight

lines.text: The World Government covers up Roger's involvement completely and buries Garp's role under a flattering lie instead.

shot.search: Government covers Roger buries Garp truth
shot.fallback: officials rewriting history for convenience

lines.text: That lie turns Garp into the so-called Hero of the Marines, a title Garp himself resented for the rest of his life.

shot.fallback: reluctant hero burdened by a false title

lines.text: Garp hated being forced into a story that wasn't true. Garling never showed a single moment of that same discomfort.

shot.fallback: two very different reactions to false glory

lines.text: Garling, on the other hand, gets declared the official champion of God Valley. Chapter 1086 confirms the title stuck.

shot.fallback: noble celebrated as an official hero

lines.text: The Rocks Pirates themselves disband after that fight, their surviving members scattering to build legendary crews of their own.

shot.fallback: crew scattering after their captain falls

lines.text: Newgate, Linlin, Kaido, all of them choose never to talk about what really happened on that island.

shot.fallback: legendary figures keeping a shared silence

lines.text: That silence is exactly why the official story, Garling's version, gets to stand unchallenged for decades afterward.

shot.fallback: convenient silence protecting a false record

lines.text: Nobody left alive on that island has any real reason to correct the record now, and everybody left standing in power has every reason to leave it alone.

shot.fallback: silence benefiting everyone still in power

lines.text: From there, his career only climbs. He becomes Supreme Commander of the entire Knights of God.

shot.fallback: noble commanding an elite order

lines.text: By chapter 1125, Garling is promoted again, this time into one of the Five Elders themselves.

shot.fallback: noble ascending to ultimate authority

lines.text: That makes him the second-highest authority in the entire World Government, beneath only Imu.

shot.fallback: powerful figure near the very top

lines.text: He even receives secret orders to replace Saint Saturn's duties, orders the other Elders aren't told about at all.

shot.fallback: mysterious orders elevating one figure quietly

lines.text: Nobody at the top ever asks why. In a government built on family name and obedience, a quiet order from above is reason enough.

shot.fallback: hierarchy accepting authority without question

lines.text: Meanwhile, King Harald spends the rest of his life carrying guilt over refusing to help Rocks when it still could have mattered.

shot.fallback: grieving king burdened by old guilt

lines.text: Harald breaks off his own horns afterward and pledges himself to the same government that ran the hunt in the first place.

shot.fallback: giant king binding himself to a system

lines.text: Garling never once looks back at any of it. Guilt was never a cost he was ever going to pay.

shot.search: Garling never looks back no guilt
shot.fallback: unburdened noble moving forward freely

lines.text: Compare that climb to Garp, who was offered Admiral again and again and turned it down every time, refusing to serve the Nobles directly.

shot.fallback: principled hero rejecting advancement repeatedly

lines.text: One man built his entire legend on refusing power he didn't earn. The other built his on taking credit for power he didn't...

shot.search: Garp refuses Garling takes credit contrast
shot.fallback: two very different relationships with power

lines.text: So ask yourself honestly: how much of Garling's power was ever really his, and how much was just borrowed from Imu?

shot.fallback: power questioned as borrowed, not earned

lines.text: People will say Garling clearly is powerful in his own right, strong enough that even Dragon's Revolutionary Army stays wary of him.

shot.fallback: respected noble feared by a rival army

lines.text: That's fair, and it's true. Nobody hands you command of the Knights of God for being weak.

shot.fallback: genuinely powerful figure acknowledged honestly

lines.text: But strength was never actually the deciding factor in Garling's promotions. Loyalty to the right people, at the right moment, was.

shot.fallback: political loyalty outweighing raw strength

lines.text: Every single promotion traces back to one pattern: be useful to whoever holds the most power, and let someone else do the hardest part.

shot.search: Pattern useful power someone else hardest part
shot.fallback: opportunist benefiting from others' effort

lines.text: Rocks did the fighting. Garp and Roger did the actual defeating. Garling simply arrived last and signed his name to it.

shot.search: Garling signs name others did work
shot.fallback: opportunist claiming credit for others' effort

lines.text: Decades of that exact same pattern are what finally put him in the Room of Authority, sitting beside Imu himself.

shot.fallback: noble finally seated among ultimate power

lines.text: That's the exact same man who, decades later, has his own fellow Noble executed just for showing commoners mercy.

shot.search: Garling later punishes Noble for mercy
shot.fallback: ruthless noble punishing a rare act of kindness

lines.text: He watches that whole execution from a comfortable chair, surrounded by cheering Celestial Dragons, like it's entertainment.

shot.fallback: noble relaxing while watching cruelty unfold

lines.text: That single image alone tells you everything you need about what kind of man actually got rewarded after God Valley.

shot.search: Image reveals rewarded man true nature
shot.fallback: telling image exposing someone's true nature

lines.text: The system never punished Garling once, for any of it. It just kept promoting him, one convenient moment at a time.

shot.fallback: corrupt system rewarding convenient cruelty

lines.text: Compare his whole career to Dragon's: one man rounds up civilians and climbs, the other breaks ranks over it and gets branded a traitor.

shot.search: Dragon branded traitor Garling climbs contrast
shot.fallback: two men punished in opposite directions

lines.text: The World Government never once mixed up which kind of man it actually wanted to keep rewarding, year after year.

shot.fallback: system knowing exactly what it values

lines.text: Even his own son Shanks gets treated as a prize to be reclaimed, not a person Garling ever actually missed.

shot.search: Shanks treated as prize not missed
shot.fallback: father valuing status over his own child

lines.text: Fifteen years ago, when Shanks finally does return to Mary Geoise, Garling is thrilled, but for the wrong reason entirely.

shot.search: Garling thrilled wrong reason Shanks return
shot.fallback: father excited for the wrong reasons

lines.text: He assumes Shanks suffered a lifetime of hardship in the Lower World and tells him he can have anything he wants now.

shot.search: Garling assumes Shanks suffered offers anything
shot.fallback: father assuming suffering, offering material comfort

lines.text: After Fisher Tiger's assault on Mary Geoise not long after, Garling personally introduces Shanks to Harald, already talking up high expectations for him.

shot.fallback: father showcasing a son like a trophy

lines.text: Harald, still carrying guilt over Rocks, has no idea he's meeting the son of the very man who finished what he refused to stop.

shot.fallback: unknowing king meeting a tangled legacy

lines.text: Garling tells him to forget everyone from his life on the surface, as if an entire childhood were simply disposable.

shot.search: Garling tells Shanks forget surface life
shot.fallback: father dismissing an entire childhood

lines.text: He never once asks Shanks whether he was actually happy down there. The question never even occurs to him.

shot.search: Garling never asks if Shanks happy
shot.fallback: father incapable of imagining his son's joy

lines.text: And somewhere out on the Grand Line, the son he once abandoned in a treasure chest grew up to become everything Garling's entire world fears most.

shot.search: Shanks grows up opposing Garling world
shot.fallback: emperor pirate standing against his own father's world

lines.text: Garling led God Valley from start to finish, and the World Government never once punished him for it. It just kept promoting him.

shot.fallback: noble's true legacy finally laid bare

lines.text: And if you want to see what Garling's own son does with that same family name, the Shanks story, that's the next one.

shot.fallback: emperor pirate walking toward his own legend
